evidence: Cic. Fin. 3.3: nec … quicquam implicātum aut tortuōsum (Lewis & Short, s.v. implicō)
terms.comment: Literally “folded in, entwined”; of a question, a speech or an affair, complicated. Gellius has implicātissima quaestiō.

evidence: Cic. Or. 102: rēs involūtās dēfīniendō explicāre (Lewis & Short, s.v. involvō)
terms.comment: Literally “wrapped up”: complicated because hidden, hard to make out.

evidence: Liv. 35.14: perplexum Pūnicō astū respōnsum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Not in Cicero or Caesar; Livy uses it of obscure, ambiguous words (Lewis & Short). It does not mean “perplexed” of a person.

evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.136: alvus est multiplex et tortuōsa (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Complex in the sense of made of many folds or parts; also “many times as great”.

phrases.latin: nec in Torquātī sermōne quicquam implicātum aut tortuōsum fuit
phrases.english: and in what Torquatus said there was nothing complicated or twisted
an answer made intricate with Carthaginian cunning
It’s more complicated than I thought.
